gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · 2-2-D02

## Step 01 · Generate candidates from dried slices and the drying scene

**Action:** Observe the food items inside the bamboo sieve and the background; try search queries such as `dried radish rings Japan` and `丸い 穴 干し 大根`. First retain both directions of dried fruits and dried root vegetables, then look for descriptions of raw materials and processing steps.

**Evidence Observation:** Inside the bamboo sieve are orange-brown, shriveled, unevenly thick round slices; many slices show holes in the center. The background features a blurred pole-mounted drying rack. The color, round shape, and wrinkles are not unique to any specific ingredient; the holes may relate to coring or stringing. There is no packaging text that directly provides the name, and the region cannot be inferred solely from the drying scene.

**Result of this step:** Use the combination of "dried round slices + central hole + string-drying" for retrieval, focusing on checking perforated dried radish while retaining similar foods for comparison.

## Step 02 · Locate the name using the same finished-product photo on the producer's page

**Action:** Check the production steps on the "ひっぽのへそ大根生産組合" page, find the image accompanying "(5) Completion, Shipping," and verify its actual image link.

https://hesodaikon.mystrikingly.com/

https://custom-images.strikinglycdn.com/res/hrscywv4p/image/upload/c_limit%2Cfl_lossy%2Ch_1440%2Cw_720%2Cf_auto%2Cq_auto/1285427/9bf1c3e3-1053-4e67-9a99-4d8f45e97dbd_hld7gn.jpg

**Evidence Observation:** The saved text from the producer's page and the recorded image link attribute this image to the completion and shipping step of Heso daikon (へそ大根). The original image corresponds exactly to the input's bamboo sieve, the position and shape of each round slice, the binding thread on the sieve rim, and the background drying rack; it is the same finished-product photo. The saved form of this page is text extracted by a web tool; the original HTTP fetch once returned a 403 error. This does not affect reading the correspondence between the saved text and the image, but it must not be written as if the original HTML was successfully downloaded again in this instance.

**Result of this step:** A direct source for the original image of the specific name now exists: Heso daikon (へそ大根). Continue to verify exactly which raw material and processing state it is, avoiding mistaking a recipe name for the name of the dried product shown in the image.

## Step 03 · Verify raw materials and name hierarchy using processing steps and official introductions

**Action:** Compare the producer page's description of the process from radish harvesting to slicing, boiling, stringing, and drying; then read the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries entries for "凍み大根" (shimi daikon) and "へそ大根のにしめ" (Heso daikon nishime).

https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/traditional-foods/menu/simidaikon.html

https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/heso_daikon_no_nishime_miyagi.html

**Evidence Observation:** Official materials classify Heso daikon (へそ大根) as a type of 凍み大根 (shimi daikon), explaining that radish round slices are boiled, strung, and naturally dried through repeated night-freezing and day-thawing in winter; the holes relate to stringing. These are processes clearly recorded in the sources; it cannot be claimed that the freezing process was observed solely from the finished-product photo. "へそ大根のにしめ" (Heso daikon nishime) is a simmered dish made using this dried product; the input presents the dried product at the shipping stage, not the re-boiled state after rehydration shown in recipes.

**Result of this step:** The name in the original image aligns with independent official raw material descriptions; the target can be determined as the specific dried product Heso daikon (へそ大根), rather than the generic term "dried radish" or a completed simmered dish.

## Step 04 · Compare truly similar dried fruits and perforated dried radish

**Action:** Use the saved photos of dried apple slices and dried apricots as appearance neighbors; then consult the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries materials on Shimane dried radish and Hida kan-dried radish to test whether the holes are sufficient for exclusive identification.

https://www.bellavivawholesale.com/products/apples-sweet-certified-organic-7-lb-box

https://www.bellavivawholesale.com/products/apricots-certified-organic-15-lb-box

https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/hoshidaikonnonishime_shimane.html

https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/38_27_gifu.html

https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/img/gifu_27_3.jpg

**Evidence Observation:** Reference images of dried apples show darker peel edges; reference images of dried apricots show shriveled depressions, but the fruit slices visible in the foreground still have flesh in the center. These are merely characteristics of the already-verified photos and cannot be expanded into fixed rules for all apple slices or apricots. The more similar Shimane dried radish is also round-cut, perforated, and strung; actual images of Hida kan-dried radish are likewise orange-brown, shriveled, perforated round slices, and the main text describes boiling, stringing, and repeated freeze-thaw cycles that are all close to the target. Therefore, appearance and basic processing alone cannot exclude these radish neighbors; the specific name in this question is ultimately established by the attribution of the producer's original photo.

**Result of this step:** Retain the similarity to neighbors; do not fabricate a false claim of a "unique hole shape." The tracing of the original image and the raw material description are already sufficient; there is no need to traverse dried goods from other regions.

## Step 05 · Output the specific name of the ingredient

**Action:** Answer using the Japanese name consistent with both the original producer and official materials.

**Evidence Observation:** The name is more specific than the category "凍み大根" (shimi daikon); if providing a Chinese explanation, one may describe it as traditionally naturally freeze-thaw dried radish slices, but it must not be explained as industrially vacuum freeze-dried, nor is it necessary to add the place of origin, which the question does not require.

**Result of this step:** Stop retrieval.

**Formal Answer:**

Heso daikon (へそ大根)
